sections.title: In brief
sections.text: The companion to “Six Types” examines five questions for each grammar class.

sections.title: Question or aim
sections.text: Which practically useful questions about a grammar are answerable or solvable?

sections.title: Approach described
sections.text: The paper studies each question against the six classes previously defined through restrictions on rule format and ordering.

sections.title: What the abstract supports
sections.text: The abstract identifies a class-by-question analysis motivated by design constraints as well as theoretical interest.

sections.title: What remains unverified
sections.text: Only the official abstract was reviewed. It does not enumerate the five questions or state their individual answers; no decision table or algorithmic guarantee is invented here.

sections.title: Why it may help
sections.text: Read “Six Types” first. Classification and decidability are different tasks: identifying a class is not itself an answer to every question about its designs.
